thread:
Jordan: quick sync on canary/A-B fallback design. proposing edge runtime + central policy combo.
Mina: summary?
Jordan: runtime = minimal, config-only hard-fails (5xx bursts, huge p99). central = richer signals, graded actions.
Sanjay: agree, no sync calls in hot path. runtime should validate a signed policy-hash only.
Ellie: how to avoid drift?
Jordan: runtime fetches signed deltas, uses checksum; on mismatch -> safe-route to golden and alert.
Mina: runtime signals: p95/p99, recent 5xx count, oom, queue depth. central signals: eval regressions, cohort metrics, tickets.
Priya: need per-tenant SLA in blob so enterprise tenants get stricter bands.
Alex: define soft-divert = mirror + tiny live sample (0.5-1%), mirrors exempt from billing.
Sanjay: DSL must be tiny: thresholds + action enum (mirror, sample, route:fallback, hold).
Ellie: add hysteresis: require 2 windows to escalate, min-enforce 5m to avoid flip-flop.
Jordan: fallback chain = ordered list; runtime probes health and tries next. final fallback = minimal stateless model + alert.
Alex: observability fields: policy_version, rule_id, decision_reason on every decision. save small counterfactual samples.
Priya: Console presets (conservative/balanced/aggressive) + raw JSON for infra. pilot toggle to opt tenants in.
Jordan: rollout phases: 1) runtime evaluator + compact blob; 2) central policy + console + pilot; 3) signal fusion, budget optimizer, counterfactuals.
Alex: i'll draft runbook snippets (policy-diff, recent-decisions). Mina/Sanjay prototype DSL + checksum. Ellie spec session-lease behavior. Priya templates + presets. Jordan will write RFC follow-up.

notes: This thread is a compact architecture follow-up discussing runtime vs central policy, DSL, hysteresis, fallback chains, and rollout phasing.
